properties.IncidentOverview: A lightning storm moved through Eastern Oregon on July 15; 2026; igniting multiple fires. The Egypt Fire was discovered on the morning of July 16; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone responded promptly but were spread thin due to several other starts in the area. Southern Area Team 2 took command of the Egypt Fire on July 19 at 6 AM. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

properties.Location: Six miles NE of Riley, OR
properties.IncidentOverview: A storm moved through northern Harney County on July 22; 2026; yielding hundreds of positive lightning strikes. The Second Flat Fire was discovered on the afternoon of July 24; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone and the Egypt Fire responded promptly but were unable to contain the fast moving wildfire as it spread over twelve miles in seven hours. Southern Area Team 2 is responsible for management of the fire; along with the Stubble; Crater; Bald Mountain and Jackass Butte fires. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

U.S. Wildland Fire Service wildland firefighters are responding to the Island Fire; which was reported on July 25 at approximately 9 p.m. The fire is located about 25 miles southwest of Ehrenberg; Arizona; in the Cibola National Wildlife Refuge. The cause of the fire is under investigation. The fire is estimated to be approximately 3;145 acres and is 65% contained. The reduced acreage is due to more accurate mapping. Wildland firefighters are actively working to suppress the fire and protect life; property; and natural and cultural resources. Closures: The Cibola National Wildlife Refuge’s Island Management Unit is closed to the public and Hart Mine Road is closed at the refuge boundary. The bridge on Hart Mine Road crossing the Colorado River collapsed into the river. Pedestrians; motorists; and boaters should avoid the area.

Daily Update (pdf) | Daily Map (pdf) The Castle Fire was first reported on July 22; 2026. It is currently estimated to be 1;727 acres. California Complex Incident Management assumed management of the Fire on Tuesday; July 28. This team will be integrated with an International CIMT from Australia. Fire Activity: Over the past 24 hours; crews have done significant work to improve and reinforce containment lines for upcoming elevated fire weather. The fire is primarily burning needle litter and small trees in the understory. Firefighter operations are primarily focused on keeping fire within its current containment lines north of Castle Rock Fork and east of the road in Black Rock Fork. Firefighters are using firing operations to stop fire spread and fight fire on their terms for safety reasons. Area Closures: A portion of the Umpqua National Forest is closed near the Castle Fire (Little Black Rock and Castle Creek areas); as well as South Umpqua Falls Campground and Day Use Area. The purpose of this Order is to protect public and firefighter health and safety during active wildfire suppression operations. Visit the Umpqua Alerts and Notices page at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/alerts/castle-fire-closure - You may also click on the Closure Order (pdf) and Closure Order Map (pdf). Public Use Restrictions: As of Friday; July 24; 2026 the Umpqua National Forest moved to Public Use Restrictions (PURs) Stage 2 across the whole Forest. Campfires within Forest Service-constructed concrete or metal fire rings within designated developed recreation sites are exempt. More Information is available at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/alerts/public-use-restrictions-stage-2 Smoke Impacts: With a significant number of fires burning within Oregon; please take steps to protect yourself from smoke. Smoke can irritate the eyes and lungs and worsen some medical conditions. People most at risk include infants and young children; people with heart or lung disease; older adults and pregnant people. Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on weather. Check current conditions on the U.S. Interagency Wildland Fire Air Quality Response Program ; the Oregon Smoke Information Blog ; DEQ’s Air Quality Index ; or by downloading the free OregonAIR app on your smartphone. About the Forest: The Umpqua National Forest protects 982;510 acres of forest across Douglas; Lane; and Jackson Counties. High Cascades glaciation; whitewater rapids; and explosive volcanic events have shaped the Forest's spectacular scenery and abundant natural resources. Verdant stands of hemlock; fir and cedar transition to forests of mixed conifers and hardwoods at lower elevations; while alpine ecosystems dominate high peaks like Mount Thielsen. The Forest's waterways and diverse ecosystems create desirable habitat for many species of fish and wildlife; in addition to providing outstanding recreational opportunities to our local communities and visitors.

An aggressive full-suppression strategy is being implemented for the Hat Fire to protect communities; structures; critical infrastructure; and other valuable resources at risk. Efforts are focused on minimizing impacts on public; private; and state lands; as well as natural and cultural resources. This is being done in coordination with the local Rangeland Fire Protection Association (RFPA) and cooperating agencies. Current Situation: Yesterday; firefighters made significant progress in reinforcing the containment lines for the Hat Creek Fire; which is now 50 percent contained. Today; their primary focus remains on mopping up hotspots and extinguishing any burning or smoldering vegetation. Smoke may be visible from smoldering vegetation well within the fire area; and firefighters will monitor for potential trouble spots. Weather and Air Quality: The large high-pressure dome anchored over the Desert Southwest will slowly shift into the Great Basin; bringing warm temperatures; low relative humidity; and increased fire behavior. Wildfire smoke will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. For more information on Air Quality at your location; visit www.airnow.gov for real-time data. Cooperating Agencies : Juntura RFPA

properties.Location: 25 Miles CW of Jordan Valley, OR
properties.IncidentOverview: An aggressive full-suppression strategy is being implemented for the Big Grass Fire to protect communities; structures; critical infrastructure; and other valuable resources at risk. Efforts are focused on minimizing impacts on public; private; and state lands; as well as natural and cultural resources. This is being done in coordination with the local Rangeland Fire Protection Association (RFPA) and cooperating agencies. Current Situation: Over the past few days; the Big Grass Fire; which is burning through brush and grass; has exhibited extreme fire behavior; with rapid rates of spread; especially in the afternoon when winds pick up. Yesterday; the primary concern remained the northeast perimeter; where strong afternoon winds and severe fire conditions pushed the fire front towards Boulder Creek with moderate to rapid rates of spread. Today; crews will continue to focus their efforts on the advancing fire in the northeast; around Boulder Creek; and in the southeast; near the North Fork of the Owyhee River. Additional firefighting resources will arrive today; including air resources (water-dropping helicopters and air tankers) to help attack the advancing fire. Evacuations: The Owyhee County Sheriff has issued a Level 3 GO evacuation order for Pleasant Valley; South Mountain; Jordan Valley; ID; Flint Creek Road; Triangle Area (including Triangle Reservoir); the West portion of Mud Flat; Juniper Mountain; and Pleasant Valley. A Level 2 SET status has been issued for Silver City . Please monitor the Owyhee County Sheriff’s Office Facebook page for changing conditions and updates. BLM Area Closure: Access to the North Fork Campground along Juniper Mountain Road in Owyhee County is temporarily closed. The entire area south of Trout Creek Road and Silver City Road to the East Fork and Main Stem of the Owyhee River and from the Oregon border east to Highway 78 and Highway 51 is temporarily closed. This closure is necessary to ensure the safety of both the public and firefighters involved in suppression efforts. Weather and Air Quality: The large high-pressure dome anchored over the Desert Southwest will slowly shift into the Great Basin; bringing warm temperatures; low relative humidity; and increased fire behavior. Wildfire smoke will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. For more information on Air Quality at your location; visit www.airnow.gov for real-time data. Cooperating Agencies: Jordan Valley RFPA; Owyhee RFPA; Malheur County Sheriff’s Office; Owyhee County Sheriff’s Office.
